title: Cocoa shells, husks, skins and other cocoa waste; coffee husks and skins

review.classification: UNSD CPC 3.0 39150 includes cocoa shells, husks, skins and other cocoa waste as well as coffee husks and skins. This association covers only the whole preheated bean-shell fraction from the declared separation stage. Agricultural pod material, whole-roasted shell supply, fuel services, extracted or carbonised products are excluded.
review.primary_evidence: JB Foods’ 2012 prospectus printed pp. 67 and 93–95 documents both preheating/winnowing and a distinct choice between selling waste and using shells as biofuel in its own boiler. It does not prove a sale to an external boiler. The ICCO processing overview distinguishes whole-bean from nib-roasting routes. Verify contemporary lot, historical burdens, receiver acceptance and actual supply state independently.
review.measurement: Net mass Q is shell material at the receiving gate with its measured moisture, nib or germ carryover and foreign material. It cannot be replaced by dry matter, energy or shipment after first acceptance. Separate mass and environmental burden accounting for beans, nibs, shell and residues, for startup losses and for any returned energy. Distinct purchases, first non-purchase receipts and same-item returns close each PP sack, paper sack and pallet ledger.
review.readiness: The specific shell product and site exchanges, actual lot state, source and receiver qualities, heat and material links remain to be confirmed. Price, zero-burden status and substitution of another fuel are not defaults. Candidate methodology and aligned Chinese retain the requirement for independent scientific and translation review.
review.original_native_records: Fixed public XML confirms the Mass to Units of mass to kg chain. The Technical Energy property points to version 01.00.000 of the energy group, while the archived group inspected is version 03.00.003. Metered MJ/kWh is independent of a specific supplier or its reference property. No site-specific product identity is inferred from either unit chain.
